items.title: Food insecurity and pain burden in patients with multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis: A comparative case-control study.
items.abstract: BackgroundFood insecurity (FI) is strongly associated with chronic disease diagnoses, pain, and functional decline. Patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have been reported to experience some degree of FI.AimsTo assess and compare the prevalence of FI in patients with MS and RA and examine associations between FI, disease severity, disability, and pain.MethodsA comparative case-control design was adopted, including 40 patients with MS and 40 patients with RA. FI was assessed using the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale (HFIAS), and pain was evaluated using the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI). Disease severity was measured using the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) for MS and the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints (DAS28) for RA. Group comparisons were performed, and multivariable regression analyses were conducted to examine associations between FI, pain, disease activity, and demographic factors.SummaryFI was identified in 65% of patients with MS and 37.5% of those with RA ( p  = 0.014). Patients with MS had greater odds of exhibiting FI compared to those with RA ( p  = 0.028). In multivariable analyses among patients with MS, greater disability was associated with increased FI ( p  = 0.019). In contrast, among those with RA, disease activity was not associated with FI. In pooled sample analyses, greater FI was independently associated with both pain severity ( p  = 0.027) and pain interference ( p  = 0.009). Overall, FI is prevalent among patients with MS and RA, with a greater prevalence observed in MS. Greater FI was consistently associated with increased pain severity and interference. These findings highlight the importance of routine FI screening and tailored nutritional and social support interventions in vulnerable populations.

items.title: Phloretin Ameliorates Rheumatoid Arthritis by Suppressing HIF-1α-Dependent Angiogenesis and Modulating of the Autophagy-Apoptosis Balance.
items.abstract: Phloretin (PHL) is an effective monomer component of Phellodendri Chinensis Cortex, Spica Prunellae, and fleshy fruits and exerts therapeutic effects on rheumatoid arthritis (RA). However, the underlying mechanism is yet to be elucidated. Following PHL treatment, therapeutic benefits were evaluated in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model using arthritic markers and joint pathology. Network pharmacology, transcriptomics, Western blotting, IHC, molecular docking, Biacore, and cellular thermal shift assay were employed. PHL administration considerably reduced joint swelling, synovial hyperplasia, and bone erosion. Integrated network pharmacology and transcriptomic analyses identified the hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α) axis as a critical target. In vitro experiments indicated that PHL effectively inhibited TNF-α-induced fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) proliferation, migration, invasion, and glycolytic reprogramming, promoted apoptosis, and suppressed excessive autophagy. Furthermore, in a coculture system, PHL substantially attenuated FLS-induced tube formation in human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Furthermore, PHL demonstrated high affinity for HIF-1α and accelerated the degradation of HIF-1α protein. Importantly, HIF-1α overexpression reversed PHL's inhibitory effect. RA severity was alleviated in Hif1a +/- mice, validating HIF-1α's pathogenic role in disease progression. PHL exerts anti-RA effects by targeting HIF-1α to modulate glycolysis and the autophagy-apoptosis balance in FLS, thereby inhibiting synovial angiogenesis. These findings provide a strong foundation for developing and applying PHL as a potential therapeutic agent for RA.

items.title: IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10, IL-17 and IL-22 secretion capacities and activation profile of T cells in psoriatic arthritis patients under disease-modifying antirheumatic drug therapy.
items.abstract: While biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) have transformed management, achieving complete remission remains a challenge due to complex immune networks in Psoriatic arthritis (PsA). This study aimed to characterize the functional modulation of circulating T-helper (Th) and cytotoxic T (Tc) cells in PsA patients following conventional synthetic (csDMARD) and biologic therapy. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were collected from bDMARD-naïve PsA patients at baseline and six months after initiating csDMARD (primarily methotrexate, n=8) or bDMARD (primarily certolizumab, n=11) therapy. Using an optimized flow cytometry-based assay, we evaluated the secretion capacities of TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-17, IL-22, and IL-10, alongside activation markers (CD40L, ICOS, CD38) in CD4 + Th and CD8 + Tc cells. Results were associated with clinical disease activity indices (DAPSA, BASDAI, PsAID-12, LEI). Both therapies significantly improved clinical scores yet failed to achieve immunological quiescence. A central finding was a significant increase in the percentage of TNF-secreting Th and Tc cells post-therapy, which may reflect a compensatory change in T-cell cytokine secretion following treatment. In the bDMARD cohort, Tc cells exhibited a significant expansion of subsets secreting IFN-γ, IL-17, and IL-10, suggesting a possible shift toward Type 1/Type 17-related cytokine responses. Baseline IL-17 and IL-10 levels correlated positively with high disease activity (BASDAI/PsAID-12), while post-treatment IL-17 and IL-22 secretory potential was specifically associated with persistent enthesitis (LEI scores). Despite clinical efficacy, DMARD therapy was associated with persistent alterations in T-cell cytokine profiles, including IFN-γ- and IL-17-producing T-cell populations, particularly within the CD8+ compartment. These findings suggest that peripheral immune profiling may provide additional insights into the immunological effects of therapy and could contribute to future personalized approaches for monitoring immune responses in patients with PsA.

items.title: Parenchymal Neuro-Behçet disease with heterogeneous clinical presentations: a comparative case report.
items.abstract: Neuro-Behçet disease (NBD) is a rare but potentially disabling manifestation of Behçet disease (BD). Its heterogeneous neurological presentation can mimic central nervous system infection, cerebrovascular disease, inflammatory demyelination or intracranial tumors, making early diagnosis difficult. Importantly, there is still limited published data on NBD from Palestine regarding presentation, diagnosis, imaging and management. We describe two patients with a long history of recurrent oral and genital ulceration who were diagnosed with parenchymal Neuro-Behçet disease (P-NBD). The first patient was a 26-year-old man with a two-week progressive headache, fever, vomiting, and blurred vision, which resembled meningitis, in whom examination showed central facial weakness, gait imbalance and pathological laughter. The second patient was a 41-year-old woman with a two-year history of gait imbalance and dysarthria who presented with three days of dizziness, horizontal nystagmus, central facial weakness, right lower-limb weakness, and a positive bilateral extensor plantar response. Laboratory testing and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were performed to exclude other differential diagnoses. Both received intravenous methylprednisolone followed by an immunosuppressive agent. The first patient had clinical and radiological improvement after corticosteroids and initiation of induction cyclophosphamide, with clinical improvement on follow-up. The second patient improved significantly on imaging after infliximab maintenance therapy. She also improved clinically, but chronic symptoms of gait imbalance and dysarthria were still present. These two cases illustrate the variable presentation of P-NBD, including a meningitis-like febrile syndrome with pathological laughter and an acute-on-chronic brainstem syndrome. In patients with recurrent oro-genital ulceration and unexplained brainstem or diencephalic neurological findings, NBD should be considered after careful exclusion of other disorders. Early diagnosis and immunosuppressive treatment can lead to substantial clinical and radiological improvement.

items.title: Candidate molecular endotypes and dynamic risk prediction in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease: a systematic scoping review.
items.abstract: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis (anti-MDA5+ DM) spans pulmonary states from no detectable interstitial lung disease (ILD) to rapidly progressive ILD (RP-ILD). We mapped molecular programs and prediction evidence to determine how recurrent biological states may support dynamic stratification. PubMed, Web of Science, Ovid and Embase were searched from inception to 22 August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR; evidence was synthesized across molecular and prediction domains. Of 4, 166 records, 2, 317 remained after deduplication, 349 underwent full-text assessment, and 95 sources (80 primary studies and 15 syntheses) were included. Type I/III interferon signaling was the most reproducible program. Myeloid inflammatory-remodeling, adaptive activation with lymphocyte or natural-killer-cell loss, vascular-coagulation injury, and immunometabolic disturbance formed additional overlapping axes aligned with pulmonary-state transitions. Clinical and radiomic models showed strong short-term discrimination; harmonized landmarks, calibration, geographic validation, and decision-timed molecular sampling would strengthen clinical use. The evidence supports an integrated map linking recurrent molecular programs to dynamic pulmonary risk. A calibrated clinical-imaging backbone, augmented by parsimonious molecular modules with incremental value and updated at prespecified landmarks, offers a practical framework for prospective endotype validation and treatment-aware prediction in anti-MDA5+ DM-ILD. https://doi.org/10.37766/inplasy2026.10.0018, identifier INPLASY2026100018.

items.title: Exercise, physical activity, and physical fitness in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis: an umbrella review.
items.abstract: Exercise, physical activity, and physical fitness are increasingly discussed in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis (PsA), but the evidence base is uneven: intervention reviews predominantly concern PsA, whereas evidence for cutaneous psoriasis is largely observational or embedded in broader lifestyle interventions. This systematic review was conducted as an umbrella review of intervention effects and observational exposure-outcome associations. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261403713). PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and SPORTDiscus were searched from inception to 1 March 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by discussion and, when necessary, a third reviewer. Reporting followed PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 and PRIOR (Preferred Reporting Items for Overviews of Reviews). AMSTAR 2 (A Measurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews 2), corrected covered area (CCA), GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations), and the Ioannidis credibility classification were applied as appropriate. Nine reviews were included. Eight reviews provided PsA evidence, including interventional, descriptive, or observational findings; one observational meta-analysis concerned prevalent cutaneous psoriasis. No eligible review isolated the effect of exercise on cutaneous-psoriasis severity. Overall confidence was Moderate for one review, Low for five, and Critically Low for three. No umbrella-level pooling was undertaken because the same trials recurred across reviews, particularly in the high-intensity interval-training/cardiorespiratory cluster (CCA approximately 16.7%), and populations, outcomes, comparators, and effect measures were heterogeneous. Vigorous activity (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.67 to 0.85) and regular exercise frequency (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.82 to 0.95) were associated with lower psoriasis prevalence, both with suggestive credibility. In PsA, possible improvements in fitness, disease activity, pain, function, and body composition were based mainly on single small trials and had very low certainty. The evidence differs by disease. For cutaneous psoriasis, current findings are observational and do not establish an exercise effect on disease severity or incidence. For PsA, intervention findings are sparse, duplicated across reviews, and of very low certainty. Safety reporting was incomplete and did not permit a disease-specific conclusion. Adequately powered, prospectively registered trials with disease-specific outcomes and systematic adverse-event reporting are required. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261403713.

items.title: Mosaic KRAS variants in childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Clinical targeted sequencing identified low-VAF KRAS variants in two of 26 children with childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Both had severe inflammatory manifestations but lacked Noonan syndrome features, and neither developed persistent lymphoproliferation suggestive of RAS-associated autoimmune lymphoproliferative disease during follow-up. These findings suggest that KRAS mosaicism may contribute to the development or severity of childhood-onset SLE.

items.title: A Multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program for the Evaluation and Management of Patients With SLE and Cognitive Concerns.
items.abstract: To develop and implement a standardized, comprehensive multidisciplinary program for the evaluation and management of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and cognitive concerns that would lead to improved diagnosis and management. The Neuro-Lupus Program evaluated 50 patients with SLE referred for any neurocognitive concern over a 12-month period. A specific sequential work-up protocol was developed for standardized patient evaluation. Initial history and examination were performed by a dedicated lupus neurologist followed by referral for comprehensive neurocognitive testing. Patients with suspected mood or psychotic disorders were evaluated in a specialized autoimmune psychiatry clinic. MRI brain scans were performed in all patients. Patients with MRI evidence of inflammation or cognitive impairment were further assessed with CSF studies and FDG-PET/CT brain. Management of neuropsychiatric medications and immunotherapy was a collaboration between neurology, psychiatry, and rheumatology. Full neurocognitive evaluation revealed a previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in 46.4% of patients tested (mild 39.3%, major 7.1%), with an additional 39.3% demonstrating a normal cognitive profile with isolated weakness. MRI demonstrated white matter disease in 50% of patients and cerebral atrophy in 10%. Brain FDG-PET/CT was performed in 8 patients (16%), 7 (88%) of which were abnormal. CSF studies demonstrated normal protein and white cell counts, but 25% had elevated kappa free light chains. As a result of this program, neuropsychiatric medications were optimized in 86% of patients and 8% had an escalation in immunotherapy. This multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program model brings together neurologists, psychiatrists, rheumatologists, and neuropsychologists to standardize the approach to neurocognitive symptoms in SLE. Among the patients enrolled, this program detected previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in the majority of those tested and was associated with changes in neuropsychiatric and immunotherapy management.

items.title: Incremental Predictive Value of Dynamic Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Beyond ESR and CRP for Glucocorticoid Sparing in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Multi-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: To identify independent predictors of sustained glucocorticoid (GC) sparing in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) initiating biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs), specifically we evaluated whether the longitudinal platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (ΔPLR) trajectory provides superior prognostic value compared to conventional measurements. This multicenter retrospective study analyzed 264 patients from the Taipei Medical University Clinical Research Database. Sparing success was defined as achieving predefined dose reduction targets at month 6 and maintaining stability for ≥ 12 weeks. Candidate predictors were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by multivariable logistic and Cox proportional hazards modeling. Clinical utility was assessed using "rescue rate" analysis. Sustained GC sparing was achieved by 139 (52.7%) patients. First-line b/tsDMARD initiation was the strongest predictor (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.23, p < 0.001) of GC-sparing success. Although static baseline inflammatory markers were non-predictive, every 10% reduction in 6-month ΔPLR independently increased success odds (aOR 1.05 [inverted from 0.95 per 10% increase], p = 0.009) and significantly accelerated the sparing rate (hazard ratio [HR] 1.02, p = 0.021). Conversely, concomitant nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug use hindered success. Notably, incorporating ΔPLR into the predictive model "rescued" 16.5% of unrecognized candidates for de-escalation-patients capable of successful GC sparing who were misclassified by standard clinical models. Although static baseline inflammatory markers are nonpredictive, 6-month ΔPLR offers significant incremental prognostic value beyond conventional erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP). By identifying 16.5% of viable candidates overlooked by standard assessments, dynamic PLR monitoring offers a potential strategy to optimize precision steroid de-escalation in RA.

items.title: Bimekizumab in Chinese Patients with Active Non-Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis: 52-Week Results from the Phase 3 BE MOBILE 1 Study.
items.abstract: Bimekizumab, a humanised monoclonal IgG1 antibody that selectively inhibits interleukin (IL)-17F in addition to IL-17A, was efficacious and well tolerated to 52 weeks in patients with non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA) in the global phase 3 multicentre study BE MOBILE 1. In this pre-specified analysis, we examine in more detail the efficacy and safety of bimekizumab in the Chinese subpopulation of patients with nr-axSpA from BE MOBILE 1. BE MOBILE 1 comprised a 16-week double-blind, placebo-controlled period and 36-week maintenance period. Patients with nr-axSpA were randomised to receive subcutaneous bimekizumab 160 mg every 4 weeks or placebo to week 16; thereafter, all patients received bimekizumab. Here we report efficacy and safety outcomes to week 52 for the Chinese subpopulation. No formal statistical comparisons were made; results should be interpreted as nominal. Overall, 36/274 patients in BE MOBILE 1 were enrolled in China (bimekizumab-randomised 18; placebo-randomised 18); 32 completed week 52. A greater proportion of bimekizumab- vs placebo-randomised patients achieved Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society (ASAS) ≥ 40% response (38.9% vs 22.2%), ASAS partial remission (33.3% vs 11.1%), and Axial Spondyloarthritis Disease Activity Score < 2.1 (77.7% vs 49.7%) at week 16. By week 52, improvements were comparable between bimekizumab-randomised and placebo-randomised patients who had switched to bimekizumab. Similar trends were observed for objective signs of inflammation, spinal pain, physical function, health-related quality of life, and peripheral manifestations. To week 52, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 33 bimekizumab-treated patients (91.7%), with upper respiratory tract infection the most frequent (10 patients [27.8%]). Four patients (11.1%) had serious TEAEs; four had fungal infections (11.1%; all Tinea). No patients experienced adjudicated inflammatory bowel disease or uveitis. In patients with nr-axSpA from China, bimekizumab showed rapid and sustained efficacy improvements to week 52 and was well tolerated, consistent with the global patient population. Graphical Abstract is available for this article. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, NCT03928704.

items.title: Comprehensive regulatory network construction highlights lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA-TF interactions and key molecular drivers in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent inflammation and progressive joint damage. Although numerous molecular contributors have been reported, the integrated regulatory architecture linking coding and non-coding transcripts remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to construct a multilayer lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA-transcription factor (TF) network to prioritize candidate regulators associated with RA. Publicly available RNA-sequencing datasets from RA and control samples were retrieved from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive. Differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq2. High-confidence miRNA-mRNA interactions were obtained from miRDip, miRNA-lncRNA associations from miRNet, and TF annotations from AnimalTFDB. Functional enrichment analyses were conducted to identify overrepresented biological themes. Network topology and module structure were evaluated in Cytoscape using CytoHubba and MCODE. Integration of interaction datasets identified 179 mRNAs targeted by 93 miRNAs, of which 90 miRNAs were connected to 404 annotated lncRNAs. Twenty-five TFs were incorporated into the regulatory framework. Degree-based analysis highlighted QKI, hsa-miR-497-5p, and KCNQ1OT1 as the most connected nodes within their respective categories. Module detection revealed five densely interconnected sub-networks, indicating coordinated regulatory organization. Several prioritized elements have previously been implicated in immune or inflammatory regulation, supporting the biological relevance of the network. This integrative analysis delineates a comprehensive regulatory landscape of RA and provides a ranked set of candidate molecules for future experimental validation. Among these, CCDC6 was identified as a downregulated gene positioned within a highly connected module and linked to multiple hub miRNAs and lncRNAs, suggesting potential functional importance in RA pathobiology.

items.title: Emerging drugs in phase 2/3 and selected phase 1/2 cellular-therapy trials: a glimpse into the future of systemic sclerosis treatment.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a complex autoimmune disease that affects multiple organs. SSc is associated with the highest mortality rate among rheumatic diseases and significantly diminishes quality of life. Consequently, research efforts have focused on understanding its etiopathogenesis and on developing related targeted therapies. Over the past decade, organ-specific therapies (such as tocilizumab and nintedanib for lung fibrosis) have been introduced to manage various manifestations of SSc. However, there is a lack of approved therapies for the overall disease. Currently, many novel compounds are being further evaluated in ongoing clinical trials. This article reviews drugs currently in phase 2 and phase 3 trials and highlights the key disease mechanisms they target in SSc. Recent advances in understanding the pathogenesis of SSc have facilitated the identification of actionable molecular and cellular pathways, leading to the testing of targeted therapeutic strategies. Concurrently, increasing emphasis is being placed on patient stratification and personalised treatment approaches to optimise clinical trial design, improve treatment responsiveness, and enhance the generalisability of trial outcomes. Among emerging treatments, cellular therapies, including chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, represent a significant innovation. This paradigm shift offers substantial potential for improving outcomes in systemic sclerosis.

items.title: Dexamethasone palmitate-loaded nanodiscs target inflamed joints and suppress rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is driven by persistent joint inflammation and dysregulated adaptive immune responses, highlighting the need for drug delivery strategies that can concentrate immunomodulatory therapy at inflamed joints and disease-associated lymphatic tissues. Here, we formulated dexamethasone palmitate-loaded synthetic high-density lipoprotein nanodiscs (DXP-NDs) as a biomimetic nanodelivery platform for subcutaneous administration and inflammation-directed delivery. DXP-NDs exhibited excellent encapsulation efficiency (95.8% ± 2.4%) and maintained their ~10 nm size for 60 days during storage either at 4 °C or 37 °C. DXP-NDs downregulated MHC-II and costimulatory molecules (CD40/CD80/CD86) on bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) in vitro. In the absence of a strong antigenic signal, this costimulatory blockade significantly promoted regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation. In contrast, upon strong antigen exposure, DXP-NDs aborted productive T-cell activation, suppressing proliferation and locking T cells in an unactivated, anergic state. Following subcutaneous administration, DiR-labeled nanodiscs selectively accumulated in inflamed joints in both zymosan-induced arthritis and collagen-induced arthritis models, with joint fluorescence correlating strongly with clinical paw scores. In a murine model of zymosan-induced arthritis, DXP-NDs alleviated inflammatory joint swelling and reduced regional Th1 frequencies. In a murine model of collagen-induced arthritis, DXP-ND therapy arrested clinical disease progression and reduced systemic IL-1β levels, with additional evidence of immune remodeling in draining lymph nodes. T-cell analysis revealed reduced Th1 and Th17 frequencies, decreased effector memory T-cell populations, and increased regulatory T-cell frequencies after extended treatment. Overall, these studies demonstrate that DXP-NDs traffic to inflamed arthritic joints and lymphatic tissues after subcutaneous administration and promote coordinated anti-inflammatory and immunoregulatory effects that attenuate joint inflammation and limit disease progression in murine arthritis models.

items.title: Predicting Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis in Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy-associated Interstitial Lung Disease: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating Quantitative CT and Clinical Features.
items.abstract: The prognosis of progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD) is poor, and current strategies for predicting its development are limited. This study aimed to use machine learning to integrate quantitative computed tomography (QCT) and clinical features to predict PPF in patients with IIM-ILD. We retrospectively included 180 IIM-ILD patients, of whom 86 developed PPF. We randomly assigned patients to training and validation sets in a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and univariate analysis were employed to select the most predictive features. We independently trained 8 machine learning algorithms. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curves, area under the curve (AUC) values, and decision curve analysis. 16 key clinical features and 7 QCT variables were selected for model development. The 10 variables with the highest contribution values were subsequently selected for the PPF prediction model. The clinical variables included Krebs von den Lungen-6, interleukin-6, percent-predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 second, carcinoembryonic antigen, ferritin, CD3 + T cells, natural killer cells, and CD19 + B cells. The QCT signatures included ILD Honeycomb Volume (%) Lt Lower + Rt Lower and ILD Consolidation Volume (%) Whole Lung. Among the 8 machine learning algorithms, the Random Forest model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.680-0.925) in the training cohort and 0.943 (95% CI: 0.866-0.982) in the validation cohort. The integration of QCT and clinical features using machine learning offers a potential non-invasive approach for predicting PPF in patients with IIM-ILD. This strategy may facilitate the early identification of individuals at high risk of PPF and potentially support timely clinical intervention.

items.title: Radiographic patellofemoral differences between end-stage knee rheumatoid arthritis and matched knee osteoarthritis vary by arithmetic hip-knee-ankle-angle-defined coronal alignment.
items.abstract: To compare radiographic patellofemoral phenotypes between end-stage knee rheumatoid arthritis (KRA) and matched knee osteoarthritis (KOA), assess disease type by coronal alignment interactions, and characterize within-KRA variation by alignment and patella baja. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 669 KRA and 669 KOA knees undergoing total knee arthroplasty from 2001 to 2024. After 1:1 propensity score matching for age, sex, and body mass index, 542 matched pairs were analyzed. Patellofemoral parameters were measured on standardized lateral and skyline radiographs. Paired tests, generalized estimating equations, nonparametric tests, and adjusted regression were used. Patella baja was more prevalent in KRA than KOA (matched-pair odds ratio, 7.03; 95% confidence interval, 5.00-9.87), and Wiberg type III radiographic appearance was more frequent (39.5% vs. 11.3%; P < 0.001). KRA also showed lower Insall-Salvati index and higher lateral patellar displacement rate. All eight KRA-KOA differences remained significant in alignment-adjusted and Larsen grade 4-5-restricted sensitivity analyses (all P < 0.001). Significant disease type-by-alignment interactions were observed for Wiberg score, lateral patellar displacement rate, lateral patellar tilt angle, lateral patellar angle, and congruence angle. Differences in displacement, tilt, and congruence were greatest in valgus knees. Within KRA, Wiberg type III was more frequent in varus and valgus than neutral knees and increased across Larsen grades; within-alignment associations with patella baja were limited and non-uniform. End-stage KRA showed a distinct radiographic patellofemoral phenotype compared with matched KOA, with several between-disease differences varying by coronal alignment.

items.title: Population Pharmacokinetics of Intravenous and Subcutaneous Belimumab, and Clinical Response Prediction in Chinese Pediatric Patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) belimumab are approved in the USA, Europe, and Japan for patients aged ≥ 5 years with active systemic lupus erythematosus. In China, IV belimumab is approved for patients aged ≥ 5 years. This analysis updates the global pediatric population pharmacokinetic model by integrating data from IV and SC Chinese pediatric studies and evaluates the suitability of a 200-mg SC dosing regimen for pediatric systemic lupus erythematosus in China. This analysis utilized the previously established two-compartment model while re-evaluating the impact of potential covariates. Allometric scaling was incorporated to account for variations in body size, and other covariates were systematically assessed through stepwise selection and their relevance to pharmacokinetic parameters. To support extrapolation of the established efficacy from the IV belimumab pediatric study to SC belimumab in pediatric patients, simulations were conducted to compare pharmacokinetic exposures between the proposed SC and approved IV regimens in Chinese pediatric patients. Furthermore, to provide additional evidence for supporting dose selection in this population, clinical response was predicted using a pre-established exposure-response model. The estimated pharmacokinetic parameters for a representative Chinese pediatric patient were: clearance, 158 mL/day; steady-state volume of distribution, 3930 mL; SC bioavailability, 77.9%. Identified significant covariates included body weight (influencing clearance and volume of distribution), and baseline immunoglobulin G and albumin levels (affecting clearance). A systematic bias of -34% in drug concentrations was observed in Chinese versus global studies. This discrepancy is unlikely to stem from racial or physiological differences and may instead be attributed to study operational factors. The established exposure-response model confirmed that simulated exposures for IV and SC regimens in Chinese pediatric patients reached the plateau of the exposure-response curve. Further simulations demonstrated that both the two-weight-band SC regimen and the trial-studied three-weight-band regimen produced exposures comparable to the IV regimen in Chinese pediatric patients. This analysis supports the suitability of a two-weight-band, dosing interval-adjusted 200-mg SC regimen for Chinese pediatric patients with systemic lupus erythematosus. Compared with the three-weight-band regimen, the two-weight-band approach simplifies administration and enhances feasibility for clinical implementation. Belimumab treats systemic lupus erythematosus, a disease where the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues. While children in many countries can receive belimumab as either an intravenous infusion or a subcutaneous injection, only the intravenous form is approved for pediatric use in China. This study investigated whether Chinese children with systemic lupus erythematosus could safely and effectively use the subcutaneous form, and what the best dosing schedule would be.This study combined data from Chinese and non-Chinese children who received intravenous or subcutaneous belimumab. A mathematical model was updated to track how the drug moves through the body, and the influence of factors like body weight and blood protein levels (immunoglobulin G and albumin) was analyzed. Computer simulations compared different dosing schedules and predicted their effectiveness based on established links between drug exposure and clinical response.The results showed that a child’s weight, immunoglobulin G, and albumin levels were the main factors influencing how much belimumab stayed in the body. Chinese children had about 34% lower drug concentrations than non-Chinese children, a difference likely due to study procedures rather than biology. Simulations found that giving subcutaneous injections once a week for children weighing 40 kg or more, and once every 2 weeks for those between 15 and 40 kg, would achieve drug levels similar to the approved intravenous treatment. This study supports this simpler two-group dosing approach for Chinese children with systemic lupus erythematosus, which is expected to be as effective as intravenous treatment and more convenient for patients and healthcare providers.

items.title: Prevalence of Urinary Incontinence and Associated Factors in Women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) can compromise the pelvic floor muscles, with the possible occurrence of urinary incontinence (UI). This study aimed to determine the prevalence of UI and associated factors in women with SLE. A cross-sectional study was conducted over 12 months in women with SLE. UI was assessed using the three Incontinence Questions (3IQ), severity using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire - Short Form (ICIQ-SF), impact of urinary symptoms using the Urinary Impact Questionnaire (UIQ-7), quality of life (QoL) using the 12-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12), and functional performance using the 30-s Sit-to-Stand (SIT) and Timed Up and Go (TUG) tests. Descriptive and bivariate analyses were performed, and factors associated with urinary incontinence (UI) were investigated using Poisson regression with robust variance, with prevalence ratios (PR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05. A total of 231 women (age 47 ± 12 years) were included. UI was identified in 52% (95% CI 46.0-58.7) of the participants. In the bivariate analysis, UI was associated with age, paid employment, family income, and some clinical and obstetric characteristics. In the final multivariate Poisson regression model, lower physical and mental health scores were associated with UI (PCS PR 0.99; 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p = 0.024; MCS PR 0.99; 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p = 0.033). UI was present in more than half of the women with SLE and was associated with worse QoL.

items.title: Latent class analysis of CT-based phenotypes in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis and pulmonary involvement.
items.abstract: Pulmonary manifestations of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) are highly heterogeneous, and a standardized CT-based classification is currently lacking. This study aimed to evaluate whether latent class analysis (LCA) of chest CT findings can identify phenotypes with clinical and prognostic relevance in patients with EGPA. We retrospectively enrolled 140 patients with EGPA and pulmonary involvement between 2014 and 2025. Chest CT findings were independently evaluated by two thoracic radiologists and analyzed using LCA to identify CT-based phenotypes. Reproducibility and clinical applicability were assessed by having radiologists reassign patients to phenotypes based on LCA-derived CT patterns while blinded to the original LCA assignments. Baseline characteristics and one-year clinical and radiological outcomes were compared across phenotypes. Modified Poisson regression was used to assess clinical relapse risk. LCA identified four distinct phenotypes: bronchial (32.1%; airway-predominant abnormalities), infiltrative (20.7%; parenchyma-predominant abnormalities), mixed (14.3%; combined bronchial and infiltrative features), and nonspecific (32.9%; without a dominant bronchial or infiltrative pattern). The bronchial and infiltrative phenotypes showed more favorable short-term outcomes, whereas the nonspecific phenotype mainly showed stable outcomes. The mixed phenotype remained associated with a higher risk of one-year clinical relapse after adjustment for age, sex, and baseline treatment. Radiologist reassignment showed excellent inter- and intra-observer agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.85 and 0.87). LCA enables the identification of CT-based phenotypes with distinct clinical characteristics and short-term outcome patterns in EGPA, suggesting potential prognostic value and a practical role in clinical management. QuestionCan latent class analysis (LCA) of chest CT findings identify imaging phenotypes of pulmonary involvement in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA)? FindingsLCA identified four CT-based phenotypes (bronchial, infiltrative, mixed, and nonspecific), each characterized by distinct clinical and radiological features and short-term outcome patterns. Clinical relevanceCT-based phenotyping may help characterize pulmonary disease heterogeneity in EGPA and identify patients, particularly those with the mixed phenotype, who may require closer monitoring for clinical relapse.

items.title: Type I interferon activation in classical monocytes and GZMK+ CD8+ T cells characterises the ultrasound-negative phase of imminent rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a prototypical autoimmune disease, characterised by prolonged systemic autoimmunity before organ-specific tissue inflammation. Understanding immune mechanisms that drive the transition from systemic autoimmunity to joint-specific pathology is key to arthritis prevention. In this study, we define immune signatures in anticitrullinated protein antibodies-positive (ACPA+) at-risk individuals who imminently progress to RA, comparing those with and without ultrasound (US)-detectable subclinical synovitis. We performed single‑cell RNA sequencing and proteomic profiling on prospectively collected blood samples from high-risk ACPA+ imminent progressors (n = 22), who were further stratified by the presence or absence of US-detectable subclinical synovitis and compared them with ACPA+ nonprogressors (n=18). We found type I interferon (IFN-I) upregulation in peripheral CD14+ classical monocyte and Granzyme K protein (GZMK)+ CD8+ T cells in US-negative (USneg, n = 11) imminent progressors. In contrast, US-positive (USpos, n = 11) progressors exhibited a phenotypic shift in CD14+ classical monocytes towards interleukin 1 beta (IL1ß)+ expression and clonal expansion of GZMB+ cytotoxic CD8+ T cells. GZMB+ and GZMK+ CD8+ T cells were largely clonotypically distinct. Plasma proteomics also revealed a shift from Toll-like receptor-associated innate pathways in USneg progressors towards effector and tissue-remodelling signatures in USpos progressors. In ACPA+ high-risk individuals, IFN-I-driven activation of peripheral innate CD14+ classical monocytes and GZMK+ CD8+ T cell subsets occur before the onset of subclinical synovitis when RA is imminent. Distinct inflammatory and effector programmes, including GZMB+ CD8+ T cells clonal expansion, are associated with the onset of subclinical synovitis.

items.title: Macrophage-derived secretory Clusterin amplifies fibroblast-like synoviocyte activation through PI3K/AKT and NF-κB signaling in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Secretory clusterin (sCLU) has been implicated in inflammatory diseases, yet its role in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains poorly defined. Here, we showed that serum sCLU levels were significantly elevated in patients with RA compared with healthy controls (n = 192 RA; n = 139 HC) and were associated with disease activity. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance for RA discrimination (AUC = 0.783, 95% CI 0.730-0.837). Mechanistically, M1-polarized macrophages exhibited enhanced sCLU secretion, whereas RA fibroblast-like synoviocytes (RA-FLS) produced minimal sCLU, identifying inflammatory macrophages as an important source of extracellular sCLU. Using a Transwell co-culture system and recombinant sCLU stimulation, we found that sCLU amplified inflammatory cytokine production and promoted the proliferative, migratory, invasive, and apoptosis-resistant phenotypes of RA-FLS under inflammatory conditions. These effects were accompanied with activation of the PI3K/AKT and NF-κB pathways and were significantly attenuated by pharmacological inhibition of either pathway. Proteomic screening, surface plasmon resonance, and co-immunoprecipitation analyses identified fibronectin 1 (FN1) as a direct binding partner of sCLU although its functional contribution requires further investigation. Importantly, genetic deletion of sCLU alleviated disease severity in collagen-induced arthritis mice. Collectively, our findings identify macrophage-derived sCLU as an inflammatory amplifier in RA and suggest that targeting sCLU may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for inflammatory arthritis.

items.title: Real-world comparison of jak inhibitors and TNF inhibitor cycling in axial spondyloarthritis patients after TNFi failure.
items.abstract: This study compared drug survival and clinical outcomes between tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) cycling and switching to a Janus kinase inhibitor (JAKi) in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) patients after initial TNFi failure. This retrospective longitudinal observational cohort study included 123 axSpA patients fulfilling the Assessment of SpondyloArthritis International Society (ASAS) criteria, followed in a tertiary rheumatology clinic. After failure of the first TNFi, patients were directed to either a second TNFi or a JAKi based on clinical evaluation. Notably, JAKi therapy was considered for patients with inadequate response to one or two prior TNFi agents. Drug survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and group comparisons were made using the log-rank test. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly shorter drug survival in the JAKi group compared to the TNFi group ( p  < 0.001). In the TNFi group, higher CRP levels were associated with prolonged drug survival (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.83-0.99; p  = 0.035), while primary non-response to the first TNFi predicted earlier discontinuation of the second TNFi (HR: 2.1; 95% CI: 1.08-3.14; p  = 0.033). In the JAKi group, prior failure of two different TNFi agents was associated with a lower risk of discontinuation (HR: 0.04; 95% CI: 0.01-0.39; p  = 0.007). Following prior TNFi failure, TNFi cycling was associated with longer observed drug survival compared with JAKi therapy. However, given the retrospective design and differences in prior treatment exposure, this finding should be interpreted as a descriptive real-world observation rather than definitive evidence of comparative effectiveness. JAK inhibitors may still represent a viable option for selected refractory patients with multiple prior TNFi failures.

items.title: Network pharmacology-guided investigation of the anti-angiogenic mechanisms of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn stem in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a severe systemic autoimmune disease characterized by progressive joint destruction. Spatholobi Caulis (SC), derived from the vine stem of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn, has a long history of clinical application in traditional Chinese medicine for activating blood circulation and relieving rheumatic arthralgia. However, its pharmacological material basis and anti-angiogenic mechanisms for treating RA remain insufficiently elucidated. To systematically investigate the active constituents of SC and elucidate its anti-angiogenic mechanisms in RA using an integrated approach combining chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and in vivo experimental validation. The chemical profile of SC was characterized using HPLC-QE-MS. A network pharmacology approach-incorporating target screening, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and GO/KEGG enrichment-was utilized to predict core targets and pathways. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were performed to evaluate the binding stability between key active compounds and hub targets. Finally, the anti-arthritic and anti-angiogenic effects were validated in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model using micro-CT, H&E, immunohistochemistry (CD31), ELISA, and Western blot analysis. Additionally, to directly verify the predicted interactions, the effects of the core compound 7,3',4'-trihydroxyisoflavone (THIF) on TNF-α-induced MH7A cells were assessed. Cell proliferation, VEGF secretion, migration, and protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB were evaluated after 24 h treatment with THIF. HPLC-QE-MS identified 24 active ingredients in SC. Network analysis identified key hub targets including SRC, PIK3CB, AKT1, EGFR, and ESR1 and revealed that SC predominantly modulates the PI3K/AKT, HIF-1α, and VEGF signaling pathways. Molecular docking, MD simulations and SPR demonstrated strong binding affinities and high structural stability between core compounds (e.g., THIF, Hesperetin, Afzelechin, (-)-Maackiain) and key hub targets (e.g., PIK3CB, EGFR, ESR1). In vivo, SC administration significantly alleviated joint swelling, preserved bone morphology (increased BV/TV and BMD via micro-CT), and reduced the organ indices of the thymus and spleen. Crucially, SC remarkably suppressed synovial neovascularization (decreased CD31-positive vessels), downregulated systemic inflammatory and angiogenic cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, VEGF, TGF-α), and significantly inhibited the protein expression of SRC, STAT3, EGFR, PI3K, AKT, and HIF-1α in synovial tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that SC effectively inhibits the proliferation of MH7A cells. Flow cytometry analysis confirmed that SC significantly induces apoptosis in MH7A cells; However, this pro-apoptotic effect was alleviated upon addition of the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Further in vitro validation with the pure compound THIF showed that it dose-dependently suppressed TNF-α-induced MH7A cell proliferation, reduced VEGF secretion from 292.18 to 80.32 pg/mL, and inhibited cell migration. Western blot analysis confirmed that THIF significantly downregulated the protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB in a dose-dependent manner, directly validating the SPR binding results and demonstrating targeted inhibition of the downstream pathological signaling pathways associated with RA. SC effectively ameliorates RA progression by mitigating synovial inflammation and preventing structural joint damage. Its therapeutic efficacy is primarily driven by the suppression of pathological angiogenesis via the targeted dual-inhibition of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/HIF-1α signaling axes.

items.title: An LLM-based decision aid for collaborative decision-making in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: A multimethod evaluation.
items.abstract: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) is the most common pediatric chronic inflammatory rheumatic condition, with substantial quality-of-life impacts. Treatment selection is complex due to limited guideline evidence, and difficult trade-offs. Decisions are often solely physician driven. We evaluated the feasibility of Large Language Model-based Decision Aid (LLM-DA) designed to support collaborative rather than solely physician decision-making in JIA care. A multi-method feasibility study was conducted in accordance with the TRIPOD-LLM checklist. The aims were twofold: first, to assess the quality of the LLM-DA (OpenAI's o3 model) based on evaluations from three pediatric rheumatologists and an exploratory assessment by an LLM-as-a-Judge (OpenAI's GPT-5 model); and second, to characterize perceived value of the tool from the patient perspective through a mixed methods evaluation (n = 34). For 10 de-identified use cases, rheumatologists and LLM-Judge generated treatment recommendations and scored the LLM-DA outputs on safety, factual consistency, treatment appropriateness, and preference acknowledgment. Rheumatologists rated 97% of outputs as acceptable for safety and preference acknowledgment, 60% for factual consistency, 70% for appropriateness. Treatment recommendation agreement among all evaluators and real-world data was low at <30%. Inter-rater agreement for scores among rheumatologists was almost perfect for safety and preference acknowledgement, moderate for treatment appropriateness, and poor for factual consistency, and remained the same or improved with LLM-as-a-Judge. Variability in evaluator scoring and treatment recommendations may reflect the inherent heterogeneity in acceptable JIA treatment pathways and potential limitations in the LLM-DA's decision-making logic. Five patient themes were identified: the tool complements rheumatologist expertise, prepares patients through reflection and actionable information, builds confidence for self-advocacy, has variable value depending on the patient-physician relationship, and has potential for broader JIA self-management. These exploratory findings provide a proof-of-concept for using AI to support collaborative decision-making, while highlighting the need for future studies to determine whether LLMs can reliably support clinical practice.

items.title: Rituximab vs Azathioprine for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Maintenance Therapy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively (P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less. items.title: Rarely involved and high damage-burden joints in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: insights from the elbow, temporomandibular joint, cervical spine, hip, and shoulder.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study is to characterize clinical features, treatment patterns, and outcomes of rare and/or high damage-burden joints in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). Patients diagnosed with JIA between January 2008 and June 2025 were included in this retrospective study. Joints involved in less than 10% of the cohort were defined as "rarely involved," and joints contributing to the total JADI-A score of the cohort were defined as "high damage-burden" joints. Among 155 patients included, temporomandibular joint (TMJ) (7.7%), cervical spine (3.9%), and shoulder (1.9%) were defined as rarely involved joints. The joints contributing most to the total JADI-A score of the cohort, including TMJ (29%), elbow (29%), and hip (19.4%), were defined as high damage-burden joints. Polyarticular disease course was the most common pattern for elbow and TMJ involvement, whereas enthesitis-related arthritis was common for hip involvement. Patients with either one of these five involvements experienced more extensive involvement, more frequent articular relapses, and higher disease activity, frequent use of bDMARDs, and rarely achieved remission off medication (ROM) (p < 0.05). Polyarticular disease course and higher ESR at diagnosis were associated with higher odds of high damage-burden joint involvement (p < 0.05).  Elbow, hip, TMJ, cervical spine, and shoulder are rare and/or high damage-burden joints of JIA. These joint involvements seem to relate to higher disease activity, more extensive disease, arthritis relapses, frequent use of bDMARDs, rare achievement of ROM, and a risk for joint damage. More extensive inflammatory disease may predispose to involvement of rare and/or high damage-burden joints. • Advances in the treatment of JIA, particularly the more widespread use of biologics, have led to significant improvements in long-term outcomes. • Suboptimal results are still encountered in JIA patients, even in the "biologic era." • Temporomandibular joint (TMJ), cervical spine, and shoulder are among the least frequently involved joints in JIA, while TMJ, elbow, and hip are associated with a high damage burden. • These five joints seem to relate to higher disease activity, more extensive disease, articular relapses, frequent use of biologic agents, rare achievement of remission off medication, and a risk of joint damage.

items.title: Compartment-specific skeletal involvement in systemic sclerosis characterized by peripheral QCT and serum osteoimmune mediators: a case-control study.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is associated with increased bone fragility, yet early, compartment-specific alterations and their osteoimmunological correlates remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to assess bone status in SSc using dual X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) complemented by peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT), and to evaluate their associations with a targeted osteoimmunological biomarker panel and clinical risk scores. This prospective cross-sectional study included 40 women with SSc (disease duration ≤ 7 years from diagnosis) and 45 non-immune female controls, frequency-matched by age. Bone status was assessed by DXA (lumbar spine, femoral neck) and distal radius pQCT. Serum levels of routine bone and mineral metabolism markers, alongside a targeted panel of osteoimmunological mediators (OPG, OPN, PDGF-BB, ACP5, RANKL, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, DKK-1) using multiplex immunoassay were measured. FRAX scores were calculated to contextualize clinical fracture risk. With broadly comparable DXA-defined bone status, pQCT revealed significantly lower trabecular volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) in SSc, while total and cortical+subcortical vBMD were comparable. Routine biochemical markers showed substantial overlap between groups, whereas SSc patients exhibited a distinct osteoimmune profile with significantly elevated OPG, ACP5, RANKL, PDGF-BB, IL-6, IL-1β, DKK-1, and RANKL/OPG after FDR correction. Exploratory biomarker-bone associations did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing. In women with relatively early SSc, pQCT identified compartment-specific differences, particularly within the trabecular compartment, despite comparable DXA-defined bone status. A distinct osteoimmunological biomarker profile was also observed in SSc, providing complementary information on disease-related skeletal alterations, while specific biomarker-bone associations require further confirmation.

items.title: Effectiveness of tocilizumab monotherapy for IgG4-related disease-like features caused by idiopathic multicentric Castleman's disease: a case-based review.
items.abstract: Idiopathic multicentric Castleman's disease (iMCD) and immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) are distinct systemic inflammatory diseases that can exhibit overlapping clinical manifestations, including elevated serum IgG4 levels and tissue infiltration of IgG4-positive plasma cells. Although interleukin-6 (IL-6) inhibitors are established first-line therapies for iMCD, optimal treatment strategies for cases of iMCD with IgG4-RD-like features remain unestablished, particularly regarding whether glucocorticoids are essential or not. Herein, we report our case of iMCD with IgG4-RD-like features successfully treated with tocilizumab monotherapy. A 68-year-old female presented with dyspnea due to a recurrent laryngeal tumor, accompanied by pulmonary consolidation, mediastinal and axillary lymphadenopathy, sclerosing mesenteritis, and retroperitoneal fibrosis. Laboratory evaluation revealed elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum IgG4 levels. Although the organ involvement and elevated IgG4 levels were suggestive of IgG4-RD, and laryngeal and pulmonary specimens exhibited IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltration, histopathological examination of lymph node confirmed the diagnosis of iMCD; therefore, we diagnosed the patient with iMCD with IgG4-RD-like features. Tocilizumab monotherapy achieved rapid normalization of CRP and IgG4 levels, along with improvement of organ involvements. The patient attained long-term clinical remission without glucocorticoids. Our literature review identified 9 previously reported cases of iMCD with IgG4-RD-like features. Eight of nine cases showed an insufficient response to initial glucocorticoid monotherapy and subsequently required the addition of IL-6 targeting agents to obtain disease resolution. Together with the findings from our literature review, our case suggests that tocilizumab monotherapy may be a potential treatment option for IgG4-RD-like features caused by iMCD.

items.title: Rituximab Combined With Azathioprine for Relapsed Anti-MDA5 Antibody-Positive Dermatomyositis With Interstitial Lung Disease: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Antimelanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5) antibody-positive dermatomyositis (MDA5(+) DM) is frequently complicated by interstitial lung disease (ILD) and is associated with a high risk of relapse. Optimal management after relapse remains unclear. A 63-year-old woman presented with characteristic cutaneous manifestations of dermatomyositis and ILD without muscle involvement. She was diagnosed with MDA5(+) DM complicated by ILD and initially treated with high-dose glucocorticoids, tacrolimus, and intravenous cyclophosphamide, resulting in clinical improvement. However, after discontinuation of calcineurin inhibitor therapy due to adverse events, disease relapse occurred, characterized by worsening cutaneous lesions, progression of pulmonary infiltrates, and an increase in anti-MDA5 antibody titers. Subsequently, azathioprine was initiated, and rituximab was administered thereafter. Both clinical and radiological findings improved, and anti-MDA5 antibody titers progressively decreased. Repeated rituximab infusions were followed by stable clinical findings, allowing glucocorticoid tapering without further relapse. This case suggests that rituximab combined with azathioprine may be a therapeutic option for disease control after relapse with MDA5(+) DM-ILD.

items.title: Computational Prediction of the Therapeutic Mechanisms From the Turmeric-Pueraria-Coix Seed Botanical Formula in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by progressive synovial inflammation and immune-metabolic reprogramming. The polyphenol-rich Turmeric-Pueraria-Coix seed (TPC) formula shows therapeutic potential against RA, though its multi-target mechanisms remain uncharacterized. To explore how TPC modulates ferroptosis and oxidative stress in RA, we integrated systems nutrition network analysis with multicohort transcriptomic datasets to identify candidate targets. Ensemble machine learning algorithms and independent cohort validation prioritized key biomarkers. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations evaluated the dynamic behavior and interaction persistence of polyphenol-target complexes, and single-cell in silico overexpression and knockout analyses characterized the regulatory consequences of perturbing these targets within RA synovial networks. Analysis identified 85 bioactive phytochemicals in the TPC formula, forming a polyphenol-dominant matrix mapping to 40 RA targets. Algorithmic and cross-cohort prioritization isolated six core genes (ALOX5, CD38, CDK1, EZH2, MAPK8, and PTGS2) linked to RA synovial transcriptomic patterns, with varying predictive performance across external cohorts. SHAP analysis highlighted PTGS2, CD38, and MAPK8; however, MD simulations prioritized CD38 and MAPK8 as stable targets of coumestrol, whereas PTGS2 exhibited less dynamic stability. Single-cell perturbation analysis revealed similar regulatory responses following MAPK8 and PTGS2 modulation, whereas CD38 knockout produced a distinct network response. These findings link TPC-derived polyphenols to CD38/MAPK8 signaling and ferroptosis in RA, providing testable molecular hypotheses for experimental validation.

items.title: Host-driven citrullination of extracellular vesicle-derived microbial proteins links P orphyromonas gingivalis to rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is closely linked to citrullinated antigens and HLA-DRB1 risk alleles, yet the origin of immunogenic citrullinated peptides remains incompletely understood. While Porphyromonas gingivalis has been implicated in RA through its bacterial peptidylarginine deiminase (PPAD), previous studies using PPAD-deficient P. gingivalis in mouse RA models reported that PPAD deletion did not attenuate disease development, suggesting the existence of additional RA-promoting mechanisms. Here, we computationally evaluate a complementary mechanism in which host peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PADI4) may modify P. gingivalis -derived proteins, generating microbial neoantigens with preferential presentation by RA-associated HLA alleles. We developed a computational framework integrating known PADI4 and PPAD substrate preferences with MHC-II antigen presentation prediction. Human proteins were first stratified based on their susceptibility to PADI4 and/or PPAD-mediated citrullination, and their presentation profiles across RA risk-associated (HLA-DRB1*04:01 and 04:04) and protective (HLA-DRB1 * 13:01 and 13:02)alleles were analyzed through MHC-II binding prediction. This analysis revealed distinct presentation signatures, including (a) global risk enrichment, (b) high-affinity binding bias, (c) characteristic allelic presentation ratios. Application of these three features led to the identification of five candidate proteins with potential relevance to RA risk, including gingipain R1 and four outer membrane proteins. These findings propose a hypothesis that host PADI4-mediated citrullination of P. gingivalis proteins may represent an additional mechanism contributing to P. gingivalis -associated acceleration of RA pathogenesis.

items.title: Oral mucous membrane pemphigoid as a window to systemic autoimmunity: two cases associated with rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Mucous membrane pemphigoid is a rare chronic autoimmune bullous disease that predominantly affects mucosal surfaces and may lead to significant morbidity when diagnosis is delayed. Increasing evidence suggests that oral manifestations may serve as reliable early indicators of systemic immune dysregulation and can precede the recognition of other autoimmune disorders. We report two cases of oral mucous membrane pemphigoid associated with systemic autoimmune diseases, emphasizing that the oral cavity is a sentinel site for systemic autoimmunity and highlighting the importance of integrated diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. In the first case, a 68-year-old woman with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis presented with recurrent oral ulcerations that were histopathologically confirmed as mucous membrane pemphigoid. During follow-up, ocular involvement was identified as peripheral ulcerative keratitis related to rheumatoid arthritis, requiring adjustment of systemic immunosuppressive therapy. Switching to B-cell depletion therapy with rituximab resulted in the control of both the extra-articular rheumatoid arthritis manifestation and mucous membrane pemphigoid activity. In the second case, a 44-year-old woman presented with desquamative gingivitis and oral bullous lesions. After a biopsy confirmed mucous membrane pemphigoid, progressive sicca symptoms prompted rheumatological investigation, leading to the diagnosis of Sjögren's disease based on serology, imaging, and minor salivary gland biopsy. Treatment with azathioprine resulted in the clinical stabilization of both diseases. These cases illustrate how oral lesions may reveal or precede systemic autoimmune disease and underscore the diagnostic challenges of overlapping immune-mediated rheumatic diseases. Recognizing shared immunopathogenic pathways may enable the selection of targeted therapies that simultaneously control multiple autoimmune conditions, thereby improving disease control and reducing the treatment burden.

items.title: Differences in the clinical profile between isolated lupus anticoagulant and triplepositive antiphospholipid antibody profiles in primary antiphospholipid syndrome.
items.abstract: To compare the clinical phenotype of patients with primary antiphospholipid syndrome who have isolated lupus anticoagulant positivity versus those with triple positivity. This cross-sectional study included two cohorts from two tertiary centers in Brazil comprising patients diagnosed with primary antiphospholipid syndrome. Of 313 patients, 135 were selected and divided into two groups. A total of 99 had isolated lupus anticoagulant positivity and 36 had triple positivity. Most participants were female (58.5%) and White (61.5%), with a mean age of 50.1±12.0 years and a median disease duration of 16 (12-22) years. Both groups showed similar rates of thrombosis (93.9% in the lupus anticoagulant group versus 100% in the triple positivity group, p=0.131) and obstetric events (55.8% versus 60.0%, p=0.754). Microthrombotic and non-thrombotic event rates were also comparable. Hydroxychloroquine use was higher in the triple-positive group (36.1%) than in the lupus anticoagulant group (15.2%, p=0.008). No more severe phenotype was observed in patients with triple positivity compared with those with isolated lupus anticoagulant positivity. The mixed ancestry and demographic composition of the Brazilian population may explain differences compared with more homogeneous populations.

items.title: A critical appraisal of guidelines and recommendations for the management of ANCA-associated vasculitis.
items.abstract: We aimed to appraise 11 currently available guidelines for ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV), identify potential gaps, and provide recommendations for improvement. The guidelines were appraised using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE II) instrument consisting of 23 appraisal criteria/items across six domains (D). Four reviewers independently appraised guidelines and scaled domain scores were calculated. The average score of all guidelines was 4.5 ± 0.8 out of 7.0. Agreement between the reviewers was excellent. British Society for Rheumatology 2025 guidelines scored highest (5.8/7.0), being the only guideline unanimously recommended for use. In 'D1/Scope and purpose', all guidelines achieved high scores. In 'D2/Stakeholder involvement', major gaps were identified in the inclusion of the views and preferences of the target population (2c), with few guidelines including patient representatives, addressing patient participation, or considering patient views. In 'D3/Rigour of development', all but two guidelines received high scores. Implementation of the procedure for updating the guidelines (3 h) and for external review (3 g) was addressed poorly. In 'D4/Clarity of presentation', all guidelines except one received a high score. 'D5/Applicability' had the lowest scores due to gaps in the criteria for monitoring/auditing guideline implementation (5d), resource/cost implications (5c), lack of advice/tools for implementation (5a), and inadequate addressing of facilitators/barriers in guideline application (5a). 'D6/Editorial independence' was addressed well. Several aspects of AAV guidelines could be improved, including the inclusion of patient views and preferences, the processes for translating guidelines into clinical practice, and clearer criteria for monitoring guideline implementation and uptake.

items.title: Case Report: Upfront sotatercept-based triple therapy in high-risk systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (SSc-PAH) carries a poor prognosis, and treatment decisions are often complicated by coexisting left-heart disease, lung disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, or pulmonary veno-occlusive disease-like vasculopathy. The role of sotatercept as part of initial therapy in treatment-naive SSc-PAH has not been established. We report a 60-year-old man with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis, first recognized at referral 3 years after the onset of skin symptoms, and high-risk precapillary PAH. Careful evaluation showed no clinically significant parenchymal lung disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, or post-capillary physiology. Upfront therapy was started with macitentan, tadalafil, and sotatercept, with short-term dobutamine support for low-output hemodynamics. After 3 months, right heart catheterization showed marked improvement: pulmonary vascular resistance decreased from 12.6 to 3.7 Wood units, mean pulmonary arterial pressure decreased from 43 to 30 mmHg, and cardiac index increased from 1.50 to 2.90 L/min/m². World Health Organization functional class improved from III to II, and risk status shifted to low risk by REVEAL Lite 2, COMPERA 2.0, and the Japanese Circulation Society/Japanese Pulmonary Circulation and Pulmonary Hypertension Society 2025 model. No sotatercept-related adverse events were observed. This case documents the short-term course of upfront sotatercept-based triple therapy in carefully selected high-risk precapillary SSc-PAH.

items.title: A mixture of pomegranate peels and propolis extracts reduces inflammation associated with rheumatoid arthritis in vivo .
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic condition characterized by the infiltration of immune and inflammatory cells into the synovial membranes, which often leads to severe damage to cartilage and bone. In spite of their efficacy, drug-based therapies produce severe side effects. Therefore, there remains an unmet need for non-pharmacological treatments with a low toxicity profile and limited costs. Propolis has been used since ancient times for the treatment of wounds, ulcers, infections, eczemas, myalgia, and rheumatism. Similarly, the traditional use of all parts of pomegranate ( Punica granatum L.) is documented across Egyptian, Persian, and Chinese cultures for the treatment of infections and inflammations. This study aimed at the development of preparations containing bioactive compounds derived from propolis and pomegranate peels, inspired by traditional recipes used in rural areas of southern Italy, to validate their efficacy in counteracting the inflammation associated with RA. A preliminary screening led to the selection of the most promising preparation, composed by propolis and pomegranate peel extracts in a ratio 1:2 (Pp1:2). It underwent a complete chemical characterization by both qualitative and quantitative LC-MS analyses and was tested on a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mouse model. In vitro tests showed that Pp1:2 treatment of M1 stimulated by LPS/IFNγ reduces cell polarization; furthermore, it reverts the pro-inflammatory effects induced by IL-1β on synoviocytes. In vivo experiments, conducted by administering Pp1:2 orally to a suitable murine model, confirmed the ability of the preparation to reduce sensibly RA-like inflammatory effects, as inferred by the change observed in mice paws volume and other RA-related parameters. Furthermore, histological analyses revealed a reduction in the number of M1 macrophages in mice paws following Pp1:2 treatment, and an attenuation of the pathological remodeling of collagen IV and of ICAM-1 expression, compared to untreated controls.

items.title: Case Report and literature review: complications of the association between rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis.
items.abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis is one of the major public health issues globally. According to the World Health Organization, it is among the top 10 causes of death caused by a single pathogen. In Romania, its reported incidence rate in 2024 was approximately 60 per 100,000 people, making it the country with the highest incidence in Europe. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by the destruction of the small joints along with symmetrical distribution and multiorgan involvement. Pulmonary manifestations are more common in males with positive serology and can involve the lungs, airways, or pleura. Short-term corticotherapy may be initiated in patients with severe symptoms, and biological therapy (anti-TNF alpha drugs) may be used in those with inefficiency of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, with an increased risk for disseminated forms of tuberculosis in those with latent infection. We present the case of a 38-year-old male patient with a 5-year history of seropositive RA who was treated with methotrexate and methylprednisolone, without any prior investigations for latent tuberculosis infection or any chest radiography performed, and was admitted with severe respiratory failure. The results of thoracic computed tomography showed bilateral pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum, with pulmonary lesions suggestive of a diagnosis of tuberculosis, which was confirmed by bacteriological testing of samples. The coexistence of two severe diseases-one requiring immunosuppressive treatment and the other one favored by immunosuppression-in a country with a high prevalence of tuberculosis infection and in the absence of latent tuberculosis infection screening or periodic pulmonological assessment can lead to severe, life-threatening complications that require complex, multidisciplinary, long-term, and expensive management.
